main_text.head: De Suilla memoratu digna.
main_text.p: EX nullo animali numerosiores ganeæ dapes præparari, fuesque[?] nihil habere præter escam, tantumq; donatas à natura ad epulandum, antiquissimi[?] pariter ac prudentissimi Philosophi prodiderunt.

Itaq; iis animam pro sale datam, ne caro viuenti putresceret, Chrysippus ait. Nihil enim fere in hac pecude reperias, quod edendo non sit, suamq; propriam suauitatem repræsentet. Hinc abdomina prisci s celebrata, glandia, testiculi, vuluæ, iecinora, verrina, & nostra memoria maxime nobilitantur latera, coxæ tam priores, quam posteriores sale macerate & suffitæ pernæ dictæ & petasones, aures, pedes, coftæ, spina, sanguis & intestina ipsa, & operosum esset singula recense-re cibaria, quæ ex illis parantur. Titus Quintius ante tribunatum & prœturam consul designatus, in Chalcide apud hospitem cœnans miratus esse traditur carnium copiam varie-tatemq;, hospite vero affirmasse illas omnes suillas esse, condimentis saltem & præpara-tionib. differentes. Convenit autem inter omnes percelebres medicos, suillam boni fac-ci[?] esse, valentissimumq; omnium escarum nutrire: testantur id fossores, messores, huius-modiq; alii grauiorum operarum, hos enim, si alio cibo pascere velis, imbecilliores red-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "fuesque" (line 2 of the first paragraph) and "antiquissimi" (first paragraph) are uncertain from the scan. "fac-ci" (in "suillam boni fac-ci esse") is read with a [?]; the printed word may be "succi". The long s has been written as plain s throughout, as the rules require. The "s" in "prisci s" is taken as printed. The catchword "des." is at the foot right and completes the word broken as "red-".
